report.executive_summary: All four packages clear both client gates (quality at least 80, defects at most 5), so the round-5 fleet-charger decision again reduces to measured energy on the shared acceptance basis. The verified ladder is P2 15 kWh, P3 24, P1 44, P4 64. P2 is the client-correct winner: 9 kWh below runner-up P3 on the identical basis, with quality 95 well above the 80 gate and the lowest defect count (1 of 5, four defects of headroom). P4's 88 quality passes, but its 5/5 defect ceiling leaves zero headroom and 4.27x the P2 energy. Fallback: P3 at 24 kWh.
report.figure_caption: Archived energy-ladder illustration for WO-05: P2 15 < P3 24 < P1 44 < P4 64 kWh with P2-minimum line, gap callouts, level ratios and defect-headroom chips; reserved box empty under no-figure delivery.

recommendation.rationale: P2. All four packages qualify; P2's 15 kWh is the lowest measured energy, 9 kWh below runner-up P3 on the identical acceptance basis, with the fewest defects (1/5, four of headroom) and quality 95 well above the 80 gate. P4's 64 kWh at 4.27x with zero defect headroom cannot compete. Fallback: P3 at 24 kWh.

sections.body: The trusted table reads: P1 quality 100, defects 3, energy 44 kWh; P2 95, 1, 15; P3 91, 3, 24; P4 88, 5, 64. Both gates are satisfied by all four packages, so none is rejected. Defect headroom against the 5/5 allowance is 4 for P2, 2 for P1 and P3, and 0 for P4, which sits exactly at the ceiling — any additional defect would disqualify it. Quality functions as a gate, not a ranking score: once a package clears 80, higher quality adds no weight under the client policy.
sections.heading: Eligibility gates and defect headroom

sections.body: Measured energy orders the field P2 15 < P3 24 < P1 44 < P4 64 kWh. Every reading shares the same work-order output, load and acceptance test, so no cross-basis correction applies and the comparison is direct. Margins over the P2 minimum are +9, +29 and +49 kWh; consecutive gaps are +9, +20 and +20. Level ratios versus P2 are 1.60x (P3), 2.93x (P1) and 4.27x (P4). Margins and ratios are stated separately, correcting the wording conflation recorded as a round-4 quality slip. All energies are distinct, so the candidate-ID tie-break never engages.
sections.heading: Energy ladder, margins and ratios

sections.body: Facts are limited to the trusted table and the declared shared test basis; everything else remains a question. First, measurement uncertainty on the 15 kWh reading is unsupplied — the 9 kWh margin to P3 absorbs it only if the combined error stays below that gap. Second, cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability are unverified and excluded from ranking; only the client may admit them. Third, persistence of this acceptance basis into later work orders is unconfirmed; a changed basis requires re-measurement, not extrapolation. Fourth, P4's defect stability matters only if it becomes a fallback, and at zero headroom it is fragile.
sections.heading: Facts versus open questions

sections.body: P2 is selected on energy after the gates, with P3 at 24 kWh as fallback. Handover to the verifier and next analyst: re-run both gates from the trusted table before ranking; treat the energy column as the sole driver once eligibility is set, using candidate ID only for exact ties. Keep the P3 fallback explicit and flag zero-headroom fragility for any 5/5 candidate. Carry the standing quality item: state kWh margins and level ratios separately. Record any new defect finding against headroom before revising the ranking, and never invent costs, schedules or measurements the sources do not supply.
